description: A DJ set: a performance the DJ played, and the tracks they played in it, in order.

main.description: One per set the DJ chose to publish. The tracklist comes from what the players logged during the set, a recording of it, or tracks the DJ added by hand. Never holds file paths, history-list names or the DJ's own notes. Tracks the DJ chose not to name are present, unidentified.

date.description: The day it was played, as YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: What sort of set it was. club and festival: played to a crowd. radio: on air. livestream: streamed as it was played. mix: recorded to be listened to later.

venue.description: Where it was played: the club, festival or station.

location.description: Where the venue is: its name, city (locality) and country.

event.description: The event it was part of: a community.lexicon.calendar.event record.

with.description: Who the DJ played with, back to back.

link.description: Where people can listen to it: Mixcloud, SoundCloud, YouTube, a station's archive.

sources.description: What the tracklist came from. history: what the players logged during the set (or a log another app kept). mix: a recording of the set, with the tracks found in it and when they start. added: tracks the DJ added by hand.

track.description: One track: named (a title, usually an artist), or unidentified.

bpmCentis.description: The track's tempo as rekordbox analysed it, in hundredths of a BPM (12800 is 128 BPM).

key.description: Its key on the Camelot wheel, 1A to 12B (8A is A minor, 8B C major).

startSeconds.description: When it starts, in seconds from the start of the set (known from a recording).

unidentified.description: Not named: the DJ chose not to say what it is (an unreleased promo, an edit), so only its place in the set is published.
